cohort: Singleton births in women with connective tissue disease (n = 851) and reference deliveries from the general population (n = 2,437,110) in Norway from 1967 to 2009
finding: Adverse pregnancy outcomes were more common among women with connective tissue disease, but risks have decreased over time.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were higher in women with connective tissue disease, with adjusted odds ratios of 5.0 in the 1970s and 1.8 in the 2000s.
